source_title: GoPro, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2016
company_context: GoPro is a consumer hardware company best known for action cameras. After a high-profile 2014 IPO and strong 2015 net income, GoPro's 2016 was marked by slowing camera demand, channel and price challenges, and a costly, troubled entry into drones (the Karma), which was recalled in November 2016 due to in-flight power loss. The company swung from profit to a large loss.
business_type: Consumer electronics / action-camera hardware, sold through retail and distribution channels (channel-inventory exposed)
evidence_summary: GoPro reported a net loss of approximately $419.0 million in fiscal 2016, a sharp reversal from net income of approximately $36.1 million in fiscal 2015. The reversal reflected slowing camera unit demand, elevated operating expenses (roughly $835 million reported), and a costly drone program: the Karma launched in 2016 and was recalled in November 2016 after units lost power in flight. Reporting indicates the Karma program cost the company over $375 million. The combination of demand softening for the core camera line, price/channel pressure, and a failed adjacent-product launch turned a previously profitable hardware brand into a heavy loss-maker, illustrating a growth story that masked a deteriorating profitability and demand problem.
outcome_evidence: Swing from ~$36.1M net income (2015) to ~$419.0M net loss (2016); Karma drone recall in November 2016; significant headcount reductions during the period as the company restructured.
source_limitations: Net loss and net income figures originate from the GoPro FY2016 Form 10-K on the primary SEC EDGAR domain (sec.gov); direct WebFetch returned HTTP 403 in this environment, so figures rely on verbatim search-result snippets sourced to the sec.gov filing. The $835 million operating-expense figure and the >$375 million Karma program cost are reported figures corroborated by secondary coverage rather than re-verified line-by-line from the rendered filing.
directly_stated: Karma drone recalled in November 2016 for in-flight power loss
inferred: Core camera demand softening plus a failed adjacent product (Karma) jointly drove the swing to loss
The case represents growth-era branding masking deteriorating unit demand and profitability
why_useful_for_opsiq: Tests separation of demand_generation_failure (core product demand slowing) from strategic_capex_risk (the Karma drone bet) and quality_trust_failure (the recall). A good multi-signal case for OpsIQ to weigh which dimension dominates and to trigger adaptive re-evaluation after a failed product launch / shock event.
